steps.title: Heel post: sketch the section
steps.command: 3D Model tab > Sketch panel > Start 2D Sketch
actions: File > New > Standard (mm).ipt and save it as gate_leaf_frame.ipt.
Start 2D Sketch on the XZ Plane (the ground). Draw a circle of diameter 450 on the origin: this is the round back of the heel post, and the origin is the pivot axis.
Draw a rectangle from the centre of the circle, 400 along the leaf (X) and 450 wide (225 each side of X).
Add the dimensions (Sketch tab > Constrain panel > Dimension): diameter 450, 400 and 450. Click Finish Sketch.
steps.note: Every gate size comes from the brief: a 4.2 m opening, 6 m high, holding up to 5.5 m of water. The leaf is 450 thick.

steps.title: Heel post: extrude it
actions: Click Extrude and pick both regions of the sketch (the circle and the rectangle).
Distance A: 5800 mm, upwards. Then in the Extrude dialog open Advanced and set a 50 mm start offset, so the post runs from 50 to 5850 above the cill (the bottom 50 mm is the cill seal).
Click OK.

steps.title: Heel post: make it hollow
actions: Start 2D Sketch on a Work Plane 350 mm above the base (Work Features panel > Plane > Offset from Plane).
Offset the outline 25 mm inwards (Sketch tab > Modify panel > Offset): the post is made from 25 mm plate.
Extrude the inner profile, Cut, Distance 5475 mm, upwards. Click OK.
steps.note: The bottom 300 mm stays solid: it is the bearing block that sits on the pintle.

steps.title: Heel post: bore for the pintle
actions: Click Hole and pick the bottom face of the heel post, on the pivot axis (the origin).
Simple Hole. Diameter 160 mm. Termination: Distance, 250 mm. Click OK.
steps.note: The 150 mm stainless pintle fits in this bore with a bronze bush: the leaf turns on it.

steps.title: Heel post: top journal
actions: Start 2D Sketch on the top face of the heel post. Circle, diameter 200, on the pivot axis. Finish Sketch.
Extrude 150 mm upwards. Click OK.
steps.note: The anchor collar (the top hinge) fits round this journal.

steps.title: Mitre post
actions: Sketch on the XZ Plane: a rectangle from X = 2160 to X = 2860, 450 wide. Extrude from 50 to 5960 mm.
Make it a hollow box: sketch the inner rectangle (25 mm walls, ending 90 mm before the mitre) and Extrude Cut.
The extra length past 2460 is trimmed to the mitre angle at the end.

steps.title: Horizontal girders
actions: Start 2D Sketch on a Work Plane at X = 400 (the face of the heel post).
Draw the eight T sections: web 20 thick from the downstream flange to the skin, flange 200 x 20, at heights 150, 800, 1450, 2150, 2900, 3750, 4700, 5860 mm.
Extrude all eight profiles 1760 mm along X, to the mitre post. Click OK.
steps.note: The girders are closer together near the bottom because the water pressure grows with depth: p = 1000 x 9.81 x depth, about 54 kPa at 5.5 m.

steps.title: Vertical stiffeners
actions: Sketch on the XZ Plane at Z = 50: two rectangles 15 wide (X 980 to 995 and 1565 to 1580), between the flange and the skin.
Extrude them up to 5960 mm. Click OK.
steps.note: The stiffeners split the skin plate into panels about 580 x 630, which keeps the plate stress low.

steps.title: Skin plate
actions: Sketch on the XZ Plane: a rectangle 12 mm thick on the chamber (upstream) face, from X = 400 to 2860.
Extrude from 50 to 5960 mm. Click OK.
steps.note: The 12 mm skin plate on the chamber face holds back the water.

steps.title: Actuator bracket
actions: Sketch on the skin plate face: a rectangle 100 wide (centred 1000 mm from the pivot) and 200 high (5700 to 5900).
Extrude it 125 mm out from the skin. Click OK.
steps.note: The electric actuator rod eye bolts to this bracket.

steps.title: Trim the mitre end
actions: Click Work Features panel > Plane > Angle to Plane around Edge. Pick the end face of the mitre post and the vertical edge where the leaf centre line meets X = 2460. Angle 18.43 degrees (1 in 3).
Click Split. Split Tool: the new work plane. Choose Trim Solid and pick the side beyond the mitre to remove.
Click OK. Save gate_leaf_frame.ipt.
steps.note: Both leaves are cut at 1 in 3 so they meet at the mitre, pointing upstream. The water pushes the mitre faces together.

steps.title: Oak fenders: one fender
actions: File > New > Standard (mm).ipt and save it as oak_fenders.ipt.
Sketch a 150 x 200 rectangle on a Work Plane at X = 500, against the skin plate face, with its centre at 2600 mm high.
Extrude it 1610 mm along the leaf. Fillet the four long edges, radius 20 mm.
steps.note: FSC certified oak: a sustainable, replaceable rubbing face for boats.

steps.title: Oak fenders: pattern them
steps.command: 3D Model tab > Pattern panel > Rectangular Pattern
actions: Click Rectangular Pattern and pick the fender.
Direction 1: the Y axis (up). Count 3. Spacing 900 mm. Click OK.
Save oak_fenders.ipt.
steps.note: Fenders at 2.6 m, 3.5 m and 4.4 m cover the water levels a boat sits at as the lock fills and empties.

steps.title: Walkway and handrail
actions: File > New > Standard (mm).ipt and save it as walkway.ipt.
Sketch a 1760 x 450 rectangle on the XZ Plane and Extrude 40 mm: the galvanised grating.
Sketch three circles, diameter 48.3, near the downstream edge and Extrude 1100 mm: the handrail posts.
Sketch two circles diameter 48.3 on a plane square to the leaf and Extrude 1608 mm: the mid rail and top rail.
steps.note: The walkway lets the lock keeper cross the lock and look at the moving parts.

steps.title: Seals
actions: File > New > Standard (mm).ipt for each seal: cill_seal.ipt (85 x 50 strip under the chamber face, trimmed at the mitre with Split), heel_seal.ipt (30 x 80 strip down the back of the heel post) and mitre_seal.ipt (30 wide strip on the mitre face).
Use the material EPDM rubber (Manage tab > Styles Editor if it is not in your library).
steps.note: Three seals stop water passing the gate: along the cill, behind the heel post in the quoin, and between the mitre posts.

steps.title: Put the leaf together
actions: File > New > Standard (mm).iam and save it as gate_leaf.iam.
Place gate_leaf_frame.ipt and right click, Place Grounded at Origin.
Place the fenders, walkway and seals. Constrain each with Mate (face to face) and Flush, using the sizes above.
Check with Inspect tab > Interference > Analyze Interference: no parts should overlap.
